The Playground

A page to write programs in the proposal's syntax, see what they compile to, and run them on Web Workers that share memory.

The playground is a page where you write programs in the proposal's syntax, see what they compile to, and run them on Web Workers that share memory. Its source is in playground/.

Using the Playground

Pick a program from the Program menu and edit it in Monaco. As you type, the page compiles the program and shows you:

  • The JavaScript. Direct field access shows what the compiler emits where TypeScript proves an object is an instance of a shared struct: the field is read and written in shared memory, without the Proxy. Proxy only shows the same program with every field access going through the Proxy. The runtime's calls are marked, and the direct accesses are in bold.
  • The errors. These are TypeScript's, from seeing each struct as a class, and the structs' own: a shared struct can't have methods, for example. They appear as squiggles in the editor and in a list.
  • The output. Run calls the program's main(workers) on a worker, with the number in the Workers field. main may block, on Atomics.Mutex.lock for example. A program starts its own workers with run(import.meta.url, 'name', ...args) from @arv/structs/agent, which calls the function it exports as name on a new worker. Their console output comes back to the page. Stop ends the run, along with the workers it started.

Monaco's TypeScript can't parse struct, so the editor only colors and completes. The errors you see come from the playground's compiler.

The page remembers your edits to each program in this browser. Reset puts the original back.

Run It Locally

You need Node 22.13 or later and a recent Chrome. A static build also needs Go 1.27 or later, and git. 

vp install
vp dev playground

On the dev server, programs compile in Node, on TypeScript's native API. Add ?wasm to the address to compile in the browser instead.

Static Builds

Without a dev server, the page compiles programs itself. It runs the same compiler, in a worker, on tsgo (stock TypeScript 7.1) compiled to WebAssembly, in a worker of its own. The two talk over pipes in shared memory. You get the same JavaScript and the same errors as on the dev server. The catch is size: tsgo is 46 MB, about 10 MB gzipped, and the page shows the download as it goes. 

vp run build-wasm
vp build
vp run test-build

build-wasm builds tsgo from TypeScript's sources at the commit of the compiler's typescript package, into public/compiler/. vp build builds the page into dist/, to be served from /playground/ (set BASE for another path). test-build serves the build with no COOP or COEP headers, so the service worker has to isolate it. It then compiles and runs every program in Chrome, in both modes, and checks that the JavaScript, the errors and the output match the dev server's.

Cross-origin isolation

SharedArrayBuffer needs a cross-origin isolated page, which takes the COOP and COEP headers. The dev and preview servers send them. Where a host can't, as on GitHub Pages, a service worker adds them, and the page loads once more under it.

Programs

Each program exports main(workers):

  • Structs: sealed, initialized in one shot, with brand-checked methods
  • Shared structs across workers: a linked list that workers add to
  • Atomics.Mutex: workers counting together
  • Atomics.Condition: a bounded queue between producers and a consumer
  • Atomics on fields: claiming work with compareExchange
  • N-body: direct field access against the Proxy
  • The mistakes the compiler catches

Layout

Path What It Is
index.html, main.ts The page, built on Monaco
boot.ts The page's entry: it isolates the page, then loads main.ts
programs/ The page's programs
compile-program.ts A program compiled, on the dev server and in the browser alike
vite.config.ts The dev server, which compiles programs, and the headers
wasm.ts, compiler.ts Compiling in the browser: the page's side, and the compiler's worker
link.ts A compiled program as a blob: module its workers can import too
tsgo/ tsgo in WebAssembly, and the API client's channel to it
build-wasm.ts, test-build.ts Building tsgo, and the static build tested in Chrome
public/coi-sw.js The service worker that isolates the page where the host can't
